kitty_graphics.value: Full core implementation behind the C API (build feature kitty_graphics, on by default). Actions q, t, T, p, d, f, a, c. Media: direct, file, temporary file, shared memory (file/temp/shm are opt-in per terminal; temp is restricted to a directory the embedder names). Formats: RGB (24), RGBA (32), PNG (100) — PNG only if the embedder installs a decode callback, otherwise rejected. zlib compression (o=z), inflated before storage. Placements: direct (anchored to tracked page-list pins), virtual (U=1) and relative (P/Q parent chains). Deletes a, i, n, c, f, p, q, r, x, y, z with upper-case freeing variants. Query and transmit replies go out through the WRITE_PTY callback. z-index with BELOW_BG / BELOW_TEXT / ABOVE_TEXT iterator filters. Animation frames (a=f, a=a, a=c) composed eagerly into RGBA; the current frame is exposed, but timed playback is driven by the Ghostty app renderer (ImageStorage.animationTick) and has no C API entry point, so an embedder sees client-driven frame changes only. Storage quota per screen (0 disables) and a 65 MiB APC buffer cap. Read side: GhosttyKittyGraphics handle, placement iterator with layer filter, image lookup returning decoded pixels plus generation stamps, and render_info geometry. Unicode placeholders: the API reports is_virtual and a per-row KITTY_VIRTUAL_PLACEHOLDER flag, but position/rect calls return NO_VALUE for virtual placements, so the embedder must decode U+10EEEE cells (diacritics, fg-colour image id) itself.
kitty_graphics.note: quote: "Before images can be stored, Kitty graphics must be enabled on the terminal by setting a non-zero storage limit with GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_KITTY_IMAGE_STORAGE_LIMIT, and a PNG decoder callback must be installed via ghostty_sys_set() with GHOSTTY_SYS_OPT_DECODE_PNG." — [measured] text from the docs group page https://libghostty.tip.ghostty.org/group__kitty__graphics.html (header lines 39-43). picture_anchoring.value: Tracked pin: each direct placement's location is a *PageList.Pin tracked by the page list, so scrolling, scrollback pruning and resize/reflow move it with the text. Virtual placements anchor through placeholder cells in the grid; relative placements resolve through the parent chain at render time. Quota: storage limit per screen (320 MB default inside the Zig storage struct; C API terminals must set a non-zero limit, 0 disables and deletes everything), plus a 65 MiB APC buffer cap for Kitty payloads.
picture_anchoring.note: quote: "Converts the placement's internal pin to viewport-relative column and row coordinates. The returned coordinates represent the top-left corner of the placement in the viewport's grid coordinate space." — [measured] ghostty_kitty_graphics_placement_viewport_pos docs. Pin type at src/terminal/kitty/graphics_storage.zig:1782-1796 ("Exactly placed on a screen pin." / `pin: *PageList.Pin`) and trackPin :2117-2121; 320 MB at :134 `total_limit: usize = 320 * 1000 * 1000, // 320MB`; limit semantics terminal.h:1350-1361.

damage_tracking.value: yes — the render state keeps a global dirty state (FALSE / PARTIAL / FULL) and a per-row dirty flag; the embedder clears both with ghostty_render_state_clean after drawing a frame. Kitty graphics add storage and per-image generation stamps.
damage_tracking.note: quote: "The render state API keeps track of dirty state at two independent layers: a global dirty state that indicates whether the entire frame is clean, partially dirty, or fully dirty, and a per-row dirty state that allows tracking which rows in a partially dirty frame have changed." — [measured] render.h:60-63; generation stamps kitty_graphics.h:87-107.

state_snapshot.value: Yes, two routes. (1) Binary snapshot: ghostty_snapshot_encode / _encode_buf / _encode_alloc and ghostty_snapshot_decoder_new / _ready / _next / _decode — 'GHOSTSNP' v1, CRC32C-framed records, a READY marker after the active screens and the unfinished VT-parser continuation, then history pages newest-first so a client can render before scrollback arrives. Format v1 is WIP with no compatibility guarantee; the C API landed 2026-08-03, so it is absent from crate 0.2.1 and present on libghostty-rs master. (2) VT formatter: ghostty_formatter_terminal_new with GHOSTTY_FORMATTER_FORMAT_VT re-encodes the screen as VT bytes with optional extras (cursor, SGR, OSC 8, protection, kitty keyboard, charsets, palette, modes, scrolling region, tabstops, pwd) — the route zmx takes through the Zig API. Neither route carries Kitty image or placement state.
state_snapshot.note: quote: "A snapshot is an ordered, CRC-protected record stream. Its READY marker follows enough state to render and resume the terminal, including any unfinished VT parser input. Older scrollback pages follow READY and the FINISH marker terminates the complete snapshot." — [measured] snapshot.h:27-30. Image exclusion: src/terminal/snapshot/grid.zig:1234-1235 "Kitty image and placement state is not part of this snapshot version". Formatter extras formatter.h:41-93. API date: `gh api "repos/ghostty-org/ghostty/commits?path=include/ghostty/vt/snapshot.h&per_page=100"` oldest = 2026-08-03 "libghostty-vt: add C API for snapshotting functions"; crate 0.2.1 has no src/snapshot.rs, master does.

threading_and_loop.value: The embedder owns the read loop: libghostty-vt has no PTY layer, no event loop, no timer and no background thread; bytes go in through ghostty_terminal_vt_write, and every effect callback runs synchronously on the calling thread (no re-entrant vt_write). The C API has no internal locking; the render docs expect a lock held across render-state update. The Rust bindings make every type !Send and !Sync, so a terminal lives on one thread and talks through channels.
threading_and_loop.note: quote: "In particular, all libghostty-vt types are !Send, meaning they cannot be transferred across threads, since the C API is allowed to use thread-local state; they are also !Sync, meaning they cannot be shared across threads, since data races may occur as the C API is not guarded with mutexes or other synchronization mechanisms." — [measured] docs.rs Thread safety section (line breaks collapsed). No timer/thread: terminal docs "libghostty-vt does not create a timer or background thread."; callbacks: "All callbacks are invoked synchronously during VT writes."; lock guidance render.h:29-34.

reply_channel.value: A per-terminal WRITE_PTY callback receives every reply byte string (DSR, DECRQM, mode 2048 size reports, Kitty graphics a=q and transmit responses). DA1/DA2/DA3, XTWINOPS size, XTVERSION, ENQ and colour-scheme queries are answered by embedder callbacks that return data for the terminal to encode. With no WRITE_PTY installed, reply-producing sequences are silently dropped — so a window replica that installs none, next to a host that installs one, gives exactly-once replies by construction.
reply_channel.note: quote: "Feeds raw bytes through the terminal's VT stream parser, updating terminal state accordingly. By default, sequences that require output (queries, device status reports) are silently ignored. Use ghostty_terminal_set() with GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_WRITE_PTY to install a callback that receives response data." — [measured] ghostty_terminal_vt_write docs (terminal.h:2222-2226). Kitty replies: src/terminal/stream_terminal.zig:1910-1918 (`if (self.effects.write_pty == null) break :resp;`). That DA/size answers leave through WRITE_PTY is [inferred] from the effects table row "VT query and mode reports written back to the PTY".

td_migration.value: Large rewrite. host.rs: replace alacritty's EventLoop / Notifier / FairMutex / tty (PTY spawn, read loop, OnResize) with a TD-owned PTY and read thread that calls vt_write and takes replies from on_pty_write; libghostty has no PTY layer, and the !Send Rust types force one emulation thread per pane or a TD-owned unsafe Send wrapper over the -sys crate. socketpty.rs: its EventedPty / EventedReadWrite shim for alacritty's loop goes away; the window replica becomes a Terminal fed socket bytes with no WRITE_PTY installed. term.rs: Term / Config / EventProxy / Processor wiring and the PtyWrite, TextAreaSizeRequest and clipboard event mapping become ghostty effect callbacks. gridwire.rs: encode_snapshot (TD's own VT re-encoder) can give way to the VT formatter or the binary snapshot, and grid_hash is rewritten over RenderState rows and cells; neither snapshot route carries Kitty images, so image state needs its own host-to-window path. pane.rs: its 51 grid reads move from alacritty Grid indexing to RenderState row and cell iteration across FFI (per-cell calls or the CELLS_RAW bulk view), flags are remapped (WIDE / SPACER_TAIL / SPACER_HEAD, GhosttyStyle), and a new image layer plus U+10EEEE placeholder decoding is added. main.rs: WindowSize-based resize announcements become ghostty_terminal_resize(cols, rows, cell_w_px, cell_h_px). pane/bench.rs: fixtures rebuilt on the new types. insights: Neither of libghostty's two state-transfer routes (binary snapshot, VT formatter) carries Kitty images or placements, so TD's host-to-window replica would still need its own image channel whichever core it picks.

kitty_graphics.value: Reference implementation (kitty wrote the protocol), kitty/graphics.c. grman_handle_command dispatches t / T / q / p / d / f / a / c (graphics.c:2219-2306). Media: direct, file, temporary file and POSIX shared memory (:558-577). Formats RGB 24, RGBA 32, PNG 100 (:549); zlib o=z (:612-613). Placements: direct with cursor movement (handle_put_command, :1128), virtual placements for Unicode placeholders (:1140-1141) drawn from U+10EEEE cells (data-types.h:132, screen.c:1183), relative placements through parent chains (:1183-1203). Deletes a, i, r, p, q, x, y, z, c, n, f with upper-case freeing variants (:2137-2175). Query replies (:2233-2241), which need an image id and are written back as APC (screen.c:1605-1606). z-index layers below background / below text / above text (:1271-1273). Animation: frame load, control and compose (:1574, :1750, :2288-2298). Quota: DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT 320 MiB per screen with eviction (:27, :80, :281-297); max image side 10,000 px (:26).

picture_anchoring.value: Integer row counter per placement: each ImageRef keeps start_row / start_column, shifted by the scroll amount on every scroll and dropped once it passes the limit. On resize only a same-width vertical shrink is adjusted; placements are not reflowed when the column count changes. Virtual placements anchor through U+10EEEE placeholder cells, which move and reflow with the text. Quota 320 MiB per screen.

grid_api.value: No embedder API. Internally a Screen holds LineBufs (main, alt) and a HistoryBuf; each Line pairs GPUCell {fg, bg, decoration_fg (underline colour), sprite_idx, CellAttrs: decoration, bold, italic, reverse, strike, dim, blink, mark, width} with CPUCell {ch_or_idx (a codepoint, or an index into a text cache for multi-codepoint graphemes), hyperlink_id, next_char_was_wrapped, multicell / scale / width fields}; LineAttrs carries has_dirty_text and has_image_placeholders. Python reaches all of it through fast_data_types.

bubbles.note: libghostty's binary snapshot deliberately omits Kitty images and placements (it keeps only the U+10EEEE placeholder cells), and the VT formatter has no image extra either. A host/window split built on libghostty-vt still has to ship image bytes and placements to the window on its own channel.
bubbles.why: TD's replica model hashes and compares both sides' grids; pictures would be the one piece of state no libghostty route transfers.

bubbles.note: The published crate 0.2.1 predates the snapshot C API (added upstream 2026-08-03) and needs Zig 0.15.x; libghostty-rs master (2026-09-01, pinned to ghostty 22d13172 of 2026-08-06) has snapshot.rs and needs Zig 0.16.x. Choosing crates.io or git decides both the feature set and the toolchain.
bubbles.why: It changes build_requirements and state_snapshot depending on which one TD pins.

bubbles.note: Timed Kitty animation playback in Ghostty is driven by the app renderer calling ImageStorage.animationTick (src/renderer/generic.zig:1440); the C API has no tick entry point, so a libghostty-vt embedder only sees frames change when the client sends a=a c=N.
bubbles.why: The kitty_tags 'animation' tag for libghostty-vt overstates what an embedder gets without an upstream API addition.

bubbles.note: wterm's production libghostty-vt renderer shipped direct Kitty placements but left out Sixel, iTerm2/OSC 1337, animation, virtual Unicode placements and file/shared-memory/URL media — a real embedder's view of what the C API leaves to the host.
bubbles.why: Independent evidence that placeholder drawing and animation are embedder work, not something libghostty-vt hands over ready-made.

bubbles.note: zmx restores clients with the Zig formatter in VT mode (not the binary snapshot): scrollback first with no extras, then clear-screen, then the active area with modes, scrolling region, keyboard and screen extras; it writes OSC 7 and the title (OSC 2) itself because the formatter adds a stray NUL to pwd and has no title extra (src/util.zig:795-877).
bubbles.why: Prior art for TD's gridwire encode_snapshot, including two formatter gaps TD would hit too.

bubbles.note: libghostty-vt reports unsupported APC sequences to an UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE callback (content capture needs a non-zero GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_UNKNOWN_MAX_BYTES), and it also implements Ghostty's own Glyph Protocol APC (GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_GLYPH_PROTOCOL).
bubbles.why: The unknown-APC hook is the kind of seam the alacritty-patched-vte and ghostty-shadow options want; a hybrid could route non-Kitty APCs through it.
